findings.title: Wire can no longer satisfy ProvideAnonDBStore's new int64 parameter
findings.body: `pkg/server/wire.go:374-375` still registers `anonstore.ProvideAnonDBStore` and binds `anonstore.AnonStore` to it. The function now takes `deviceLimit int64`, and nothing in the wire set provides a bare `int64`. Wire generation fails with "no provider found for int64". Also, `AnonDeviceService` now builds its own store (impl.go:43), so nothing consumes that binding anymore, and wire would reject it as an unused provider even if the parameter were satisfied. Remove both lines from wire.go, or take the limit from `*setting.Cfg` inside the provider.

findings.title: Device limit only blocks the first request; the local cache lets later requests through
findings.body: `tagDeviceUI` writes the device key to `localCache` (impl.go:87) before it calls `CreateOrUpdateDevice` (impl.go:93). When the store returns `ErrDeviceLimitReached`, the first request fails in `Authenticate` (client.go:45-46). Every later request from the same device ID within the 29-minute cache TTL hits the cache at impl.go:83-84, gets nil back, and is authenticated as anonymous. So a device over the limit only loses one request. Set the cache entry only after the write succeeds, or delete it when `ErrDeviceLimitReached` is returned.

findings.title: Count-then-insert is not atomic, so concurrent new devices can go over the limit
findings.body: `CreateOrUpdateDevice` counts active devices and then inserts in a separate statement, outside any transaction. Several new devices tagged at the same time (possibly on different Grafana instances) can each see `count < deviceLimit` and all insert. If `device_limit` is meant as a hard cap, do the check and the insert in one transaction or in one conditional insert statement.

findings.title: Device tagging now runs on the request path
findings.body: Tagging used to run in a background goroutine with its own 2-minute timeout. Now `TagDevice` runs synchronously on each anonymous request that misses the cache. With a limit set, that adds a `CountDevices` query plus an insert or update to the request's latency, and a slow database now delays anonymous page loads directly. The error is only needed when the limit is reached, so the extra queries could be skipped when `deviceLimit == 0`. That path doesn't run the count query today, but it still does the write synchronously.

findings.title: anonymousDeviceLimit is typed as `undefined` but the backend always sends a number
findings.body: `FrontendSettingsDTO.AnonymousDeviceLimit` is a plain `int64` (frontend_settings.go:195), so the payload always contains a number (0 when unset), never undefined. Without a type annotation, the class field `anonymousDeviceLimit = undefined` gets the type `undefined`. Consider `anonymousDeviceLimit: number | undefined = undefined`, or default it to `0` so it matches what the backend sends.

contracts.action: Anonymous Authenticate now calls TagDevice synchronously and returns ErrDeviceLimitReached as an auth error
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous goroutine-based tagging in the same function
contracts.before_after: tagDeviceUI caches the device key before the DB write, so a failed write is not retried until the cache expires
contracts.visible_effect: Only the first request from a device over the limit is rejected; requests within the next 29 minutes pass
contracts.failure_mode: Other DB errors are logged and the request still authenticates; only the limit error rejects, and only once

contracts.action: ProvideAnonDBStore signature gains deviceLimit; the service constructs its own store
contracts.before_after: Wire still lists the provider and the interface binding

summary: This adds an anonymous device limit, set by `device_limit` under `[auth.anonymous]`. When the limit is reached, only devices that already exist and are still active get updated, and new devices fail anonymous auth. Blocker: `pkg/server/wire.go` still registers `ProvideAnonDBStore`, which now needs an `int64` that nothing provides, so wire generation fails. Fix: the local cache is written before the DB write, so a device over the limit is rejected on its first request and then let through for the next 29 minutes. Minor points: the count-then-insert can race and go over the limit, tagging now runs on the request path, and the frontend config field is typed as `undefined`.
